name: S. Fairbanks, land agent

proprietors.name: Seth Fairbanks
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Seth Fairbanks is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at land_agent in the south division (slot trade_households:persons/male/20_29/south/family/trade:land_agent:045), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. Here the head is not merely the proprietor of the house — the head IS what bought it, because no count of this class was ever printed to be short of.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a land office kept by a south-division household deals this house onto South Water Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the resident band drew a land agent the town was short of, and the trade names the house he keeps. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The head who keeps it is ordered onto the scene date and to nothing narrower, and a keeping is not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Seth Fairbanks (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real land office in the south division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head.

trade_head.note: A TRADE HEAD, NOT A SHORTFALL AND NOT A ROOF. The December 1835 State census's eighteen lines never reach this class, so the order book holds no bucket to point at and no count of it can be short; and nothing in data/structures/ is a land office, so there is no committed building to buy the firm either. What IS committed is the man: the resident band drew Seth Fairbanks at land agent because the 1839 trade table says the town was short of the trade, and a land agent kept an office and the register prints three houses of the trade — J. C. Goodhue, land agent; W. G. Blanchard, house and land agent, on Lake Street; and one unnamed house and land agent — against a census that enumerates no land office at all. The house is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the resident band drew 2 head(s) at land agent in the south division and a land agent kept an office and the register prints three houses of the trade — J. C. Goodhue, land agent; W. G. Blanchard, house and land agent, on Lake Street; and one unnamed house and land agent — against a census that enumerates no land office at all. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: the form the register prints this trade in twice over — 'J. C. Goodhue, land agent' and 'W. G. Blanchard, house and land agent' — which is also form 1 of the naming guide, the commonest signature in the corpus. The goods line is the trade line the register prints under J. C. Goodhue.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head himself, a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders his person bucket, or a source naming a real house of this class; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
